319574.title: Linear-degree conjecture for Tverberg graphs
319574.literal_statement: Let $q\geq 2$ be a prime power, $d\geq 1$, and let $G$ be a graph on $(d+1)(q-1)+1$ vertices. A graph is a **$(d,q)$--Tverberg graph** if it has the corresponding Tverberg property for parameters $d$ and $q$. **Linear-degree conjecture.** There is a constant $k$ such that, whenever the maximal degree of $G$ is less than $kq$, $G$ is a $(d,q)$--Tverberg graph. The conjecture proposes a substantial improvement over the sufficient bound $D(D+1)<q$; its status is unclear from the supplied text.

319656.title: Cameron–Praeger conjecture on block-transitive 6-designs
319656.literal_statement:
Let a **block-transitive $6$-design** be a $6$-design whose automorphism group contains a subgroup acting transitively on its blocks; call the design **non-trivial** when it is not one of the standard trivial designs.

**Cameron–Praeger conjecture.** There are no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-designs.

This conjecture addresses the existence of highly symmetric Steiner designs. Cameron and Praeger had already proved non-existence of block-transitive designs for $t>7$; the paper establishes the stronger result that no non-trivial block-transitive Steiner $t$-designs exist for $t=7$ or larger, while the $t=6$ assertion is the remaining conjectural case in the supplied passage.

319940.title: Sun's base- expansion conjectures
319940.literal_statement:
Let $n,m,k$ be positive integers with $m\geq 2$. For a positive integer, its base-$m$ expansion is the representation using digits from $0$ through $m-1$; a **non-zero digit** is a digit in this expansion that is not $0$.

**Sun's conjecture.** (I) There are at least $k$ non-zero digits in the base-$m$ expansion of

$$
\frac{m^k-1}{m-1}n.
$$

(II) The sum of all digits in the base-$m$ expansion of

$$
(m^k-1)n
$$
\nis at least $k(m-1)$.

These assertions generalize Sun's results for binary expansions and for prime bases, giving digit-expansion lower bounds for products involving geometric sums and $m^k-1$.

320378.title: Depth-seven conjecture for edge rings of finite graphs
320378.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph on the vertex set $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with $d\geq 7$, and let $K[G]$ be its edge ring. **Depth-seven conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{depth} K[G]\geq 7.
$$

The claim arises from computations showing that connected nonbipartite graphs with seven vertices have edge rings of depth at least seven. The preceding discussion presents it as a temptation rather than an established theorem; the supplied status gives no evidence of resolution.

321036.title: Chartrand's existence conjecture for prescribed rainbow connection numbers
321036.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $rc(G)$ and $src(G)$ denote its rainbow connection number and strong rainbow connection number, respectively. Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. **Chartrand's conjecture.** There exists a connected graph $G$ such that $rc(G)=a$ and $src(G)=b$ if and only if $a=b\in\{1,2\}$ or $3\leq a\leq b$. The conjecture asks whether the lower bound on $b$ in the preceding existence theorem can be removed; it was subsequently confirmed by Chen and Li, who constructed graphs with the prescribed parameters.

318155.title: Komlós–Sós conjecture on degree-sequence conditions for tree embeddings
318155.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $k$ be a positive integer. A tree with $k$ edges has $k+1$ vertices. **Komlós–Sós conjecture.** If at least $n/2$ vertices of $G$ have degree at least $k$, then $G$ contains every tree with $k$ edges. This conjecture is presented as a generalization of a theorem of Zhao and is part of the effort to characterize degree conditions forcing tree embeddings; the source does not report a resolution.

318840.title: Kalai's separator conjecture for simple polytopes
318840.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a simple $d$-polytope with $m$ vertices, and let $G_P$ be its graph. **Kalai's separator conjecture.** There exists a subset $V'$ of vertices of $P$ such that

$$
|V'|=O\left(n^{1-\frac{1}{d-1}}\right)
$$

and removing $V'$ from $G_P$ separates $G_P$ into two parts, each with at least $n/3$ vertices. The source presents this as a version attributed to Kalai and as a conjecture about vertex expansion; the variables $m$ and $n$ are inconsistent in the source statement, and no resolution is given.

318975.title: Eulerian descent-set distribution conjecture for marked cycles
318975.literal_statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let ${\mathcal T}^0_n$ be the class of objects defined in the paper, let $D(\sigma)\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-1\}$ denote the descent set of $\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n$, let ${\mathcal S}_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $A_n(x)$ be the $n$-th Eulerian polynomial.

**Eulerian descent-set distribution conjecture.** For any $n$ and any subset $D\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-1\}$,

$$
|\{\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n\,:\,D(\sigma)=D\}|=|\{\pi\in{\mathcal S}_n\,:\,D(\pi)=D\}|.
$$

In particular,

$$
\sum_{\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n}x^{\operatorname{des}(\sigma)+1}=A_n(x).
$$

The conjecture arose from experimental evidence and was checked by computer for $n$ up to $9$; the asserted distribution beyond those computations remains open.

318983.title: Lemke–Kleitman conjecture on indices of sequences over cyclic groups
318983.literal_statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the cyclic group of $n$ elements, let $d$ and $n$ be positive integers with $d\mid n$, and let $S$ be a sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$. For a subsequence $T$ of $S$, write $\sigma(|mT|_n)$ for the sum of the least positive representatives of the terms of $mT$, where $m$ is coprime to $n$. **Lemke–Kleitman conjecture.** There should exist a nonempty subsequence $T$ of $S$ and an integer $m$ coprime to $n$ such that

$$
d\mid\sigma(|mT|_n)\mid n.
$$

The case $d=n$ asserts that every sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$ contains a subsequence of index $n$. The paper states that this conjecture is false in general, giving counterexamples for $n=4k+2\geq22$, although related assertions hold under repetition hypotheses and are believed in some prime-order cases.

319242.title: General bias-forcing conjecture for oriented even cycles
319242.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph, let $n$ be its number of vertices, and let $e(D)$ be its number of arcs. For subsets $A,B\subseteq V(D)$, write $e(A,B)$ for the number of arcs from $A$ to $B$, and define

$$
bias(D):=\max\left\{e(A,B): A,B\subseteq V(D),\ e(B,A)\leq \frac{e(A,B)}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Even-cycle bias conjecture.** For each integer $k\geq 2$, there exists a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every oriented graph $D$ satisfying

$$
bias(D)<\varepsilon\frac{e(D)^{k/(k-1)}}{n^{2/(k-1)}}
$$

contains an oriented cycle of length $2k$.

This generalizes the paper’s proposed six-cycle bound and connects small orientation bias with the forced presence of longer even directed cycles. The source gives no indication that the conjecture is solved.

319288.title: Freeness conjecture for the sharp transform of the planar binary tree algebra
319288.literal_statement:
Let ${\bf PBT}$ be the Loday–Ronco algebra of planar binary trees, and let ${\bf PBT}^\sharp$ denote its $\sharp$-transform. For each tree $T$ with at least two nodes and empty right subtree at the root, let ${\bf P}_T^\sharp$ be the corresponding sharp-transformed element.

**Freeness conjecture.** The algebra ${\bf PBT}^\sharp$ is free over the set ${\bf P}_T^\sharp$, where $T$ runs over trees with at least two nodes and such that the right subtree of the root is empty.

The claim describes a proposed free generating set for the sharp-transformed planar binary tree algebra. The supplied text gives no evidence that this assertion has been resolved.

364497.title: Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture
364497.literal_statement:
Let $0 \le k < d$ be integers, and let $r_0, \dots, r_k$ be positive integers. Suppose that $P_0, \dots, P_k$ are sets of points in $\mathds{R}^d$ satisfying

$$
|P_i|=(r_i-1)(d-k+1)+1
$$

for each $i$. **Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture.** There exists a $k$-dimensional flat $V\subseteq\mathds{R}^d$ and, for each $i$, a partition of $P_i$ into $r_i$ parts such that the convex hull of every part of every partition intersects $V$. This conjecture generalizes the central transversal theorem in the same way that Tverberg's theorem generalizes Rado's centerpoint theorem. Its topological and colorful generalizations are known when all $r_i$ are powers of the same prime $p$ and $p(d-k)=p\cdot\operatorname{codim}_{\mathds{R}}V$ is even; it remains open otherwise.

317294.title: The $\mathbb{P}_4$ characterization conjecture for matroid representability
317294.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an indeterminate, and define the partial field

$$
\mathbb{P}_4:= \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{Q}(\alpha),\{\alpha,\alpha-1,\alpha+1,\alpha-2\}).
$$

**$\mathbb{P}_4$ characterization conjecture.** A matroid $M$ is representable over all finite fields with at least $4$ elements if and only if $M$ is representable over $\mathbb{P}_4$. The statement is offered as a candidate after the preceding finite-field list conjecture could not be proved even for $k=4$; no resolution is given.

317742.title: The quantum and delta grading conjecture for the Khovanov–Heegaard Floer spectral sequence
317742.literal_statement: Let $L$ be a link, let $\Sigma(L)$ denote the double cover of $S^3$ branched along $L$, and let $\{E^k(L),D^k\}$ be the spectral sequence whose $E^2$ term is the reduced Khovanov homology $\widetilde{Kh}(L)$ and which converges to $\widehat{HF}(-\Sigma(L))$. For each $k\geq 2$, consider the page $E^k(L)$ and its differential $D^k$. **Quantum and delta grading conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$, there is a well-defined quantum grading, respectively $\delta$-grading, on each $E^k(L)$, and the differential $D^k$ increases these gradings by $2k-2$, respectively $-1$. Such gradings would refine the spectral sequence beyond its known $E^2$ and $E^\infty$ terms and clarify how the limiting grading compares with the Maslov grading on $\widehat{HF}(-\Sigma(L))$.

317975.title: The Sprouts winning-strategy congruence conjecture
317975.literal_statement: In the Sprouts game, a two-player game beginning with $p$ spots in which the player making the last move wins, a player has a winning strategy for exactly one of the two players. **Sprouts winning-strategy conjecture.** The first player has a winning strategy if and only if $p$ is congruent to $3$, $4$, or $5$ modulo $6$. This is the original pattern conjectured from computer analysis of the game; the paper studies its extension from the plane to compact surfaces, while the general status of the pattern is not resolved here.

318003.title: Bialostocki's zero-sum permutation conjecture
318003.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive even integer, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ be zero-sum sequences with terms in $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Thus

$$
\sum_{k=1}^n a_k=\sum_{k=1}^n w_k=0.
$$

**Bialostocki's conjecture.** There exists a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ such that

$$
\sum_{k=1}^n w_k a_{\sigma(k)}=0,
$$

where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\\{1,\ldots,n\\}$. The conjecture concerns pairing two zero-sum sequences so that their weighted inner product vanishes modulo $n$; the paper confirms it when the weights form an arithmetic progression with even common difference.

380331.title: The invertibility conjecture for self-complementary symmetric graphs
380331.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a self-complementary symmetric graph of order $n$, let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement, and let $G^{-1}$ denote its inverse under the graph operation used in the paper. **Invertibility conjecture.** The graph $G$ is invertible if and only if $n=1$ or $n\equiv5\pmod 8$; in that case, $G^{-1}=\overline{G}$. The statement is explicitly suggested by computer testing, while the supplied text gives no proof or disproof.

380434.title: The Hom-complex realization conjecture for diameter-one graphs
380434.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a finite simplicial complex, let $T$ be a finite connected graph, let $K_2$ be the complete graph on two vertices, and let $G_{1,X}$ be the graph obtained from $X$ by the construction in the paper with $k=1$. For a graph $H$, write $\operatorname{Hom}(K_2,H)$ for its Hom complex.

**Hom-complex realization conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{diam}(T)=1,
$$

then there is a homotopy equivalence

$$
\operatorname{Hom}(K_2,G_{1,X})\simeq X.
$$

This is the precise formulation of the proposed improvement from the general construction to the case of a complete graph with possibly some loops. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture remains open.

379622.title: Positive-coefficient conjecture for adjacent edges in independence polynomials
379622.literal_statement: Let $\mathsf K_n$ be the complete graph and let $Z(\mathbf I\mathsf K_n;\mathbf y)$ be the partition function of its independent-set system. For edges $e,f$, let $\Delta Z\{e,f\}$ denote the Rayleigh difference. **Adjacent-edge coefficient conjecture.** If $e$ and $f$ are adjacent edges in $\mathsf K_n$, then $\Delta Z(\mathbf I\mathsf K_n)\{e,f\}$ has nonnegative coefficients. The claim has been checked for $n\leq6$ and is open in general.
